name: std::next

declarations.code:
template <class InputIt>

InputIt next(InputIt it, typename std::iterator_traits<InputIt>::difference_type n = 1);

template <class InputIt>

constexpr

    InputIt
    next(InputIt it, typename std::iterator_traits<InputIt>::difference_type n = 1);

intro: Return the nth successor (or -nth predecessor if n is negative) of iterator it.

sections.title: Parameters
sections.text:
it

 -

 an iterator


 n

 -

 number of elements to advance


 Type requirements


 -InputIt must meet the requirements of LegacyInputIterator.

sections.title: Return value
sections.text: An iterator of type InputIt that holds the nth successor (or -nth predecessor if n is negative) of iterator it.

sections.title: Complexity
sections.text:
Linear.

However, if InputIt additionally meets the requirements of LegacyRandomAccessIterator, complexity is constant.

sections.title: Possible implementation
Notes
sections.text: Although the expression ++c.begin() often compiles, it is not guaranteed to do so: c.begin() is an rvalue expression, and there is no LegacyInputIterator requirement that specifies that increment of an rvalue is guaranteed to work. In particular, when iterators are implemented as pointers or its operator++ is lvalue-ref-qualified, ++c.begin() does not compile, while std::next(c.begin()) does.
